# Hive operations desk

**Release HOLD.** The decision is the reviewer’s disposition on the four Rails source heads in the [pinned Workflow #92 packet](https://github.com/mojomast/workflow/blob/2d45b5958abed555b910cbddd5bdfe5e8b22144d/evidence/rails-rc/release/DECISION.md). It is not a check on the current Hive build. The docket gives each gate a finding, source, currentness and next step. Reveal the SHA pins to compare specific heads. An unavailable provider does not prevent inspection of this public packet.

## Reading revision evidence

* `apps/rizzstack-hive/release.js` is generated by the existing digest-checking importer. Its CI observation is `2026-11-17T22:41:57.149960+00:00`. The 665 required cases and 64 component jobs are different measures. The latter apply only to the exact four-head tuple; a missing or changed SHA invalidates reuse.
* The packet includes a different repository, `fixture/r18`. In `release/offline-replay.json` (SHA-256 `30662accd36bdcfdeef9a0a86cf8f4ef19acebbae4e13f2cebb77311f180668f`), the baseline exited 1, the verified tree exited 0, and the integrated tree `f2c1f30980d7c001a2402aa316f20f03b0a3e08b` exited 0. This last SHA matches the native RETURN’s `integration.commit`, wave `r18-coding.w1`. It is neither one of the four component heads nor a hosted PR merge commit. The offline receiver verified bytes and replayed tests; the human receiver decision was pending.
* `operations.js` includes a **separate dated CLI capture**, 2026-11-18 00:19:02–00:19:05 UTC. For each `mojomast` component we read `gh api repos/mojomast/{repo}/branches/main` and `.../pulls/{number}` and then read `.../commits/{full_sha}/check-runs?filter=latest&per_page=100` for each observed main and PR head. Each check run named its respective SHA and every reported run fit on the page. These are reported check runs, not a configured required-check verdict or a new tuple gate. A captured zero means no runs were returned; skipped and in-progress runs are not passes. The reads across repositories were not atomic.

| Component | PR number / head at capture | PR check runs | Main head at capture | Main check runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow | #91 `badc5591d7e5d4985fe829c3a1e39b2ee0e4c0f6` | 14 successful | `58aa9690c2494ab0ffc37094a6c303ac09cd7510` | 14 successful |
| BundleBees | #82 `433dfa1f6ae7ada071d3ccfb0056b8a0e13b2aa0` | 0 reported | `4ed25529cc18e32e5c0161bc538aae086ae5eb89` | 3 successful, 1 in progress |
| Hyvv | #26 `35a4d0cf9473b3d30a2b8eb0b71ab9d10b6509a8` | 14 successful | `9bed64999f23d12c354c6f714b70e182f54f4486` | 14 successful |
| Orbit Desktop | #46 `43a3cb61b8e5f9822c3bcc1431afe850b8ca0c3e` | 32 successful | `9cb894b76df30b6852e7d899a3b5e82fc97eb5ee` | 10 successful, 1 skipped |

All four PRs were open, non-draft and unmerged **at the CLI observation**. The earlier #92 CI capture recorded open drafts. `merge_commit_sha` on an open PR is not a receipt of a merge; none is used. Main and PR status may have changed since. The pane does no GitHub polling. At admission, collect a fresh tuple, jobs and combined-tree evidence. Separately obtain pre-dispatch Windows worker/ledger attribution and dated operator authority, repeat HTTP and memory qualification, preflight protected historical copies, measure installed and loaded parity, rehearse rollback, and obtain the human receiver and promotion decisions.

## Available readers

| Source | What exists | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Overview and Rails | [Exact-pane host read](HIVE_INTEGRATION.md), `src/hive-host.ts`, `src/rails-shell.ts` | Owner grants a bounded snapshot. Navigation is for an observed attempt or job; the host rechecks grant, selector membership and age. A separate **Inspect history** gesture starts the shell’s bounded read. Only the shell handles credentials, query cursor and first-page stream cursor. An SSE invalidation triggers a scoped refetch. No stream or Rails query response is handed to Hive. |
| Queue and leases | BundleBees `bundlebees_plugin/hive_queue_read.py` reads bounded retained action/feature/work JSON; `work_scheduler.py` and `leases.py` own their native records. | Local/offline, not a browser provider. A feature card can name dependencies and a job. An action can name a fence and protocol revision; `done` still has `effect: unknown`. Scheduler `overlap_ids` compares recorded file keys with other **claimed rows in the same copy**. `[]` is not a free production lease; `null` is incomplete. No filenames or lease secrets are needed in Hive. |
| Draft coverage | BundleBees `bundlebees_plugin/hive_coverage_view.py` joins a feature, frozen packet, PR observation and independently pinned native RETURN. Orbit `queue-desk.js` shows one disconnected PARTIAL example. | Snapshot CI does not supply exact reviewed heads. Require exact repo/PR, observed open draft head, job, contract, named AC and matching GREEN/verifier references. No title-based joins. Missing AC means unproved coverage, not missing implementation. The adapter can suggest PARTIAL, COVERED_BY_DRAFT, IN_FLIGHT or UNKNOWN; it never changes the queue. |
| Remote stream | BundleBees `rails_remote_source.py` reads from a fixed enrolled peer into the coordinator. Separately, Workflow `contrib/rizzstack-observability/events_bridge.py` maps launcher JSONL into a gated `/obs-events` SSE stream with a bounded replay/reset window. | Neither reader enrolls Hive. The inspected Orbit host has no `/obs-events` relay. Launcher `bee.*` / `tool.progress` payloads are not canonical Rails evidence. No direct worker, remote SSE, alternate-origin or fleet-wide subscriptions. |
| Owner actions | BundleBees `rails_actions.RetryHandoff` is in-process; the coordinator rechecks policy/fence at claim and commit. Signed quality feedback is a separate opt-in trusted-shell flow. | No Hive dispatch, retry, verify, queue reconcile, pause/resume, routing, feedback, approval, merge, deploy, rollback, promotion or worker enrollment provider. A signed quality note is not a receiver decision. |

## Proposed companion read contract — not implemented

Keep queue/lease/PR observations outside frozen snapshot/1 and outside Rails event formats. This proposal is a reviewed host-to-pane projection for **one explicitly selected public subject**, not an endpoint, executable preview, general RPC or filesystem bridge. No reader or permission is installed by documenting it.

**Envelope allowlist.** Exactly `version` (literal `hive-work-read/1`), `subject` (`kind` enum `feature|work|action`, `id`), `source` (enrolled public alias), `sourceRevision` (immutable source-generation digest), `observedAt` (UTC timestamp), `quality` (`known|partial|stale|conflict|unavailable`), `truncated` (boolean) and `rows`. Each row has a discriminant and exactly the fields in its allowlist; missing facts are explicit nulls. No extension maps, raw records or display markup.

| Row kind | Permitted fields besides kind |
|---|---|
| `queue` | `id`, `repo`, `jobId`, native `state`, `at`, `dependsOn`; feature and action states stay in their own source vocabulary. |
| `lease` | `workId`, `claimId`, `at`, `expiresAt`, `fenceSeq`, `overlapIds`; only public claim identities and observed counters, never fence authority or lease filenames. |
| `pr` | `repo`, `number`, `state`, `draft`, `head`, `mergedAt`, `mergedSha`, `at`; a merged SHA requires an observed completed merge. |
| `coverage` | `featureId`, `jobId`, `repo`, `prNumber`, `head`, `contractSha256`, `returnSha256`, `greenSha256`, `covered`, `missing`, `classification`, `queueAt`, `prAt`; always a suggestion. |

**Bounds and authority.** Proposed ceiling: 64 KiB UTF-8 per response, 50 rows, 16 items per nested list, ASCII public IDs 1–128 characters, repo as two validated ID segments, Git SHA 40 lowercase hex, digests 64 lowercase hex. Use closed enums, valid UTC dates, nonnegative safe-integer counters and a fixed nesting depth. Reject unexpected/duplicate keys, malformed IDs, off-subject rows, invalid dates, private values and unknown versions **before** transfer. Truncation never proves absence. One request in flight per explicitly granted exact pane, at most one per 30 seconds, 10 s deadline. Suspend in background; discard in-flight results on scope or grant change. No raw RETURN, URL from a row, tool arguments, owner identity, private path, address, token, commands, or transcript.

**Reconciliation.** The trusted producer must establish the subject from an already-authorized exact selector and its durable source. Compare `(source, kind, scoped id, sourceRevision)`; same bytes are duplicate, divergent bytes at the same identity/revision are conflict. A revision digest is an identity, not an ordering. Ignore delayed responses from superseded read generations. Do not order independent sources by wall clock; preserve each observation time. On head/contract/fence changes discard the prior coverage or lease implication; retain history as historical. Empty/incomplete input means unknown. Join by exact repository/feature/job, PR/head, contract, AC and evidence digests. Never infer execution from queue `done`, a clear local overlap list, matching titles, or a lease ACK.

**Remote invalidation would need separate review and enrollment.** A future host-only stream adapter would accept one selected scope, a server-pinned source, an enrolled vocabulary and a bounded invalidation (`source`, public `scope`, `epoch`, `sequence`); no raw SSE or launcher `payload` delivered to Hive. One subscription, ≤1 KiB per invalidation, coalesce to the read cadence, use bounded resume with backoff. Duplicate sequence: no new work; gap, restart or reset: retire the cursor and request a bounded authoritative snapshot, preserving the gap until reconciled. Unknown origin/vocabulary: refuse. 401/403, revoke, navigation or expiry: abort, clear private state and reauthorize. Sequence/chain integrity establishes origin continuity, not dispatch attribution, verification or human acceptance. No fleet fan-out.

**Capability discovery is deny-by-default.** The shell must authenticate the principal, bind the document and scope, consult its own explicit read-provider registry and recheck on each use. No grant from plugin metadata, a caller-supplied endpoint, role, check result, projection row or function name. `controlsFor` returns a UI description only. The only recognized navigation provider is the controller’s `providers.rails` handle from `connectHost`; `mode: 'host'`, `connected: true` and a matching observed selector are also required. Writes always have `available: false` with a reason and next evidence gate; passing extra provider names cannot change this. Any future writer needs its own reviewed, owner-authorized preview/confirm/claim/commit/reconcile contract and idempotent uncertain-result recovery. Nothing here adds a transport, outgoing fetch, mutation or generic bridge.
